action: Inspected exactly one official primary source, RFC 9053, for a standalone digest/hash algorithm identification mechanism usable in a signed deterministic evidence envelope.
tested_result: RFC 9053 binds hash choice to COSE signature-algorithm identity and recommends protecting that identity against substitution, but does not itself define a standalone application-level content-digest identifier paired with arbitrary digest bytes. This exact candidate is therefore insufficient for unambiguous independent digest identification without an application profile or separate digest-identifier standard.
tested_scope: Exactly one source: RFC 9053 sections 1.3, 2.1 and 2.2 relevant to algorithm wire values, ECDSA hash identity/protected-header substitution defense, and application transport of hash content. No implementation, second source, external execution, protected-primary action, manual-user action, scheduler mutation, or cross-role/O/downstream semantic input.
conflict_check: CLEAN-safe and non-conflicting; exact tested scope preserved.
continuation: Next invocation re-bootstrap/freeze authority and reconstruct p1-sa-558, then inspect exactly one official primary source that defines a standalone digest/hash algorithm identifier namespace suitable for persisting algorithm identity next to digest bytes (prefer RFC 6920 Named Information hash-algorithm identifiers if its official text directly defines the needed identifier semantics). Test only whether a fixed {digest_algorithm_id,digest_bytes} evidence field can be interpreted unambiguously without external execution handoff. Do not inspect a second source or execute an implementation, and retain concrete Chat-native digest computation, deterministic encoding, COSE cryptographic execution, key trust, replay/freshness policy, PROV-to-JSON mapping, and observation/inference/uncertainty schema as unresolved children.
